subject.title: fix(cli-runner): use sender metadata in CLI session history user labels

question: Should CLI reseed history expose the persisted external sender identity as `User (<sender>): …` after the sanitizer is hardened, or should this boundary remain generic `User` until a different trusted presentation contract is chosen?
rationale: The code fix is narrow, but deciding whether third-party identity metadata belongs in model-visible historical context is a durable trust and product-boundary choice rather than a mechanical implementation detail.

options.title: Accept hardened attribution
options.body: Harden all Unicode line separators, retain the envelope-only fallback chain, and accept sender attribution in reseed history.

options.title: Keep generic reseed labels
options.body: Preserve the current `User` rendering and defer sender presentation until an owner-defined context contract is available.

options.title: Redirect the presentation contract
options.body: Ask for an owner-designed representation that marks sender identity as untrusted while preserving participant attribution.

recommendation.title: Accept hardened attribution
recommendation.body: Harden all Unicode line separators, retain the envelope-only fallback chain, and accept sender attribution in reseed history.

likelyOwner.reason: They introduced the persisted sender metadata contract consumed by this PR and are best placed to judge its permitted model-visible uses.
